correctness.rationale: The unique-path Markov SIR infection event has probability p^distance by independent exponential races on successive path vertices; no false assumption of global edge independence. The Prüfer bijection and AHU isomorphism encoding exhaustively generate 24 unlabeled tree classes through n=7. For 22, rational Bernstein dominance of one candidate against all vertices implies a constant full argmax set on (0,1). Exactly the two stated remaining classes have explicit polynomial gaps p(1-p)(1-p-p^2) and p(1-p)(1-2p), while exact Bernstein inequalities strictly exclude every other vertex. Standalone check.py was executed from its actual package directory; it reports counts [1,1,2,3,6,11], 18,248 code words and precisely two exceptions; these are complete finite checks, combined with analytic identities for every real p.

originality.rationale: The distance-decay score, qualitative parameter sensitivity, tree non-rooting failures and epidemic sentinel frequency measures are prior work. value.rationale: The sharp 7-vertex threshold answers a naturally posed sentinel-design question for epidemics with competing transmission/recovery scales, and distinguishes adjacent-optimum migration from nonadjacent optimal hubs joining at an intermediate site. Both crossover values translate into exact epidemiological rate ratios (golden ratio and equality), and the exhaustive eleven-shape classification is a useful finite benchmark for evaluating surveillance heuristics. This is not a generic deduction from known qualitative parameter effects or a randomly sliced numeral; order 7 is proven minimal, with precisely two morphologies. Value does not imply applicability to larger, weighted, cyclic or real empirical contact networks.
